observations: Large industrial machine with blue exterior panels and a grey structural frame.
Control interface featuring a digital display screen and physical control buttons (Photo 1).
Internal electrical cabinet containing a PLC, circuit breakers, and organized wiring (Photo 0, 2).
Mechanical interior shows pneumatic cylinders, hoses, and silver flexible ducting.
The machine is positioned outdoors on a concrete surface next to shipping containers and a truck.
A watermark 'MACO MACHINES' is overlaid on all three photos.

claims.evidence: The machine appears clean and free of obvious wear, but it is shown outdoors and unpacked, which prevents verification of 'brand new' status without documentation.
Photo 1 shows a control panel with a PLC screen and automated control components.
The internal mechanical configuration, including the heating and mold areas visible in Photo 1, is consistent with this type of machinery.

risks.proof: A video showing the machine powered on, navigating the control menus, and completing a dry cycle.

risks.risk: Missing essential auxiliary equipment (high-pressure compressor and chiller)
risks.proof: Photos of the accompanying air compressor and water chiller units.
risks.if_unproven: as the blowing unit only, requiring significant additional investment

risks.risk: Unknown production capacity and power specs
risks.proof: A clear photo of the manufacturer's metal data plate/nameplate.

proof_requests: Photo of the manufacturer's data plate showing the model, year, and technical specifications.
Video of the machine in operation or performing a dry cycle.
Photos of the air compressor and water chiller if they are included in the sale.
Photo of the preform loading system to confirm the degree of automation.
response.reason: The manufacturer's nameplate and specific model are not visible. In industrial machinery, these details define the production capacity and power requirements, which are the primary drivers of value.
